Personal Injury Billing

Beyond the Car Accident: Slips, Falls, and Every Other Injury Claim

Personal injury billing covers the wider category of injury claims beyond motor vehicle accidents: slip and fall cases, workplace injuries outside workers' comp, product liability injuries, and any case where a third party's liability, not standard health insurance, is expected to eventually cover the cost of care.

Like MVA claims, these cases usually run on a letter of protection or a lien against a future settlement, which means the practice provides care now and gets paid later, once liability is established and a settlement is reached. That gap between care and payment is where documentation discipline and case tracking either protect a practice's revenue or quietly erode it.

PMEX documents every personal injury case thoroughly from the first visit, coordinates with the attorney handling the liability claim, and tracks the case through negotiation and settlement so the provider is paid what the case is actually worth.

Questions

Personal Injury Billing: Frequently Asked Questions

A letter of protection is a document from a patient's attorney promising payment to the provider out of a future settlement, in exchange for treating the patient now without upfront payment.

MVA billing is a specific type of personal injury billing tied to auto accidents. Personal injury billing more broadly covers any injury case involving third-party liability, including slip and fall, workplace and product liability cases.

If a liability case does not result in a settlement, the provider's ability to collect depends on the specific terms of the letter of protection and applicable state law. PMEX tracks each case's status closely to flag risk as early as possible.

Documents are exchanged through HIPAA-compliant fax and email channels, with delivery and receipt confirmation, so nothing goes missing between the practice, the attorney and the insurer.

Yes. The PMEX portal shows real-time case status, so your team can check where a case stands without waiting on a status update call.
